ticket.title: Test runs write into the production telemetry log
ticket.description: The only two spans in sawhorse's telemetry log are unit-test artifacts: a provider at 127.0.0.1:59999 and DEFINITELY_NON_EXISTENT_KEY_VAR_12345. Emission fails open, so a test that exercises a failing completion appends to the real log of whatever repository it ran in. Harmless as observability noise, poison as training data: synthetic failures teach a model that a clean run is an error, and stripping them later is guesswork once the test names are gone. Suppress emission under test with an environment guard, or tag the span so downstream filters can drop it.
acceptance_criteria: running the suite tests adds no line to any telemetry log; a real run still records

events.description:
The only two spans in sawhorse's telemetry log are unit-test artifacts: a provider at 127.0.0.1:59999 and DEFINITELY_NON_EXISTENT_KEY_VAR_12345. Emission fails open, so a test that exercises a failing completion appends to the real log of whatever repository it ran in. Harmless as observability noise, poison as training data: synthetic failures teach a model that a clean run is an error, and stripping them later is guesswork once the test names are gone. Suppress emission under test with an environment guard, or tag the span so downstream filters can drop it.

FIXED AND PROVEN 2026-11-08 (commit 20213d6, common).

LIVE PROOF: sawhorse/.gaugeblock/telemetry/events.jsonl held 2 lines - both unit-test artifacts. Running the full
sawhorse-core test suite (23 tests, one of which exercises a failing provider completion) left it at 2 lines. Before
this change that run would have appended.

Two ways to stay quiet: GAUGEBLOCK_NO_TELEMETRY set to any value, or the process is a cargo test binary recognised as
target/*/deps/<name>-<hash>. The second is structural rather than name-based, so a crate called miter-tests installed
as a real binary is unaffected - and it exists because the alternative does not: this workspace denies unsafe_code and
set_var is unsafe in edition 2024, so a test cannot switch emission off for itself.

The policy sits on append_span, not append_span_forced, because a SpanGuard is built by a caller that already decided
to record. Splitting them made the existing guard tests fail for the right reason, which is how I knew which side of
the line each belonged on.

Still owed in the telemetry set: GB-338 (root the writer, delete the federating reader), GB-339 (one span per CLI
invocation across nine more tools), GB-341 (retention with tracked aggregates).
